Coverage and record classes

A missing Operational record is not proof of real-world non-adoption. Candidate, planned, construction and shutdown statuses remain distinguishable in the site details and export.

Waste quantities are US short tons. The waste year describes the quantity, not the date of the recorded project or collection status.

Exploratory statistical baseline — actual grouped holdout

Target: Operational project record versus known status without an Operational record. The 316 Unknown-only sites were excluded from modeling, not assigned a negative label.

ModelROC-AUCAverage precisionBrierRecall at 0.5

Site attributes: log10 waste quantity, operating status, ownership. The second model adds waste-record year and missingness indicators as a data-coverage sensitivity analysis. Gas collection, project type, power and flow are excluded. Imputation, scaling and category encoding were fitted on training rows only, separately for each fold.

The holdout is separated by county groups linked through shared operational projects. These are classification results for the register, not measured emissions, true non-adoption, future forecasting or causal policy estimates. Small recall at the fixed 0.5 threshold remains a practical limitation.

Additional research: geography, features and screening tradeoffs

Retrospective leave-one-state/territory-out stress test: 53 geographic folds, 2,325 known records. Every tested state was excluded from its fitted model. This is not a new external dataset, a future forecast, or a replacement for the original holdout.

Fixed feature specificationOriginal holdout APLeave-state-out pooled AP

The 316 Unknown-only records stay outside all models. State-level small samples and recording coverage limit interpretation.

Practical record-review queue: 757 collection sites without an Operational record

This is a data-verification queue, not an investment ranking, emissions estimate or recommendation to deploy a model. Mixed-status records retain every original status. Buckets use construction, planned, candidate, future potential, low potential, then shutdown; Unknown stays separate.

Verification bucketSites

Export includes names, IDs, source rows, units, all statuses and a concrete verification question per record. The underlying release is September 2024; no current-status check is claimed.

Definitions, provenance and use
  • Landfill ID is the site key. Raw project rows include expansions and multiple supplying sites. Operational project counts reconcile to 542 parent projects and 488 landfills.
  • All landfill rows match the original landfill-only snapshot on every common site field. Original raw files are preserved; no synthetic environmental records are used.
  • The database is incomplete and fields are not all updated annually. Complete-case analyses disproportionately retain open sites and sites with operational projects.
  • All calculations run in this browser. CSV export includes the current filters and source URLs. Search is a presentation filter and does not modify the source data.

Completed public-source checks: historical labels versus later evidence

Four purposive examples, not a representative validation sample. All September 2024 model labels remain frozen. A later operational report does not make the original historical label incorrect.

Site / 2024 recordLater evidenceRemaining limit
Simi Valley LF / Construction; ShutdownThe receiving utility reports accepting RNG from the new WM Simi Valley facility on 2026-01-06.Confirms a later operational-use event, not continued uninterrupted operation as of October 2026, measured emissions, or a 2024 database error.
Magnolia Subtitle D MSW LF / ConstructionThe public waste authority describes RNG production at Magnolia; a dated developer announcement links a 2026-01-14 credit sale to that landfill project.The operating page is undated, and the tax-credit transaction alone does not establish commissioning date, legal eligibility or causal policy effects.
American Avenue Landfill / PlannedThe county agenda identifies a proposed amendment of the landfill gas conditioning system permit, including changed capacity and equipment.An agenda/proposed permit amendment is not an operation or commissioning certificate; current operational status remains unresolved.
Medley Landfill / ConstructionThe contractor case study describes a completed Medley RNG facility converting landfill gas.No publication/commissioning date or exact source-project ID: retain as follow-up evidence, not a dated validated outcome.

Magnolia: official operating description is undated; address changed between office/site references. Fresno: a permit proposal is not proof of operation. Medley: contractor claim is undated and the exact project identity needs confirmation.
